localBiteReport: The most recent available report covering Choctawhatchee Bay specifically is from the week of September 4–10, 2026 (about one week old). According to that report, the bay is showing early signs of the fall transition: large schools of baitfish (greenies/menhaden) have moved from open water into bayous, flats, and bridge areas, and the flats redfish bite is described as improving and expected to strengthen further as September progresses toward October. A Santa Rosa Beach angler report posted approximately 6 days ago noted plenty of speckled trout activity and a notable bull redfish catch (a 40¼-inch, 26-lb fish) out of the bay. Water temperature at this location today is 87°F, which continues to push the best redfish and trout action to early mornings and evenings on the flats, with bait concentrations near bridge structures also worth targeting.
